title: Vendor performance and revenue impacts guideline
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Summary:
This guideline defines how vendor performance (delivery, SLAs, and invoicing accuracy) is measured and how those measurements are mapped to revenue recognition and billing controls at Redwood Inference. It provides a governance model, KPI thresholds, procurement-to-finance handoffs, and an escalation path when vendor performance could materially affect timing or amount of revenue.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all third-party vendors that supply: Dedicated capacity (GPU pools), runtime software (licensed inference components), and professional services tied to customer commitments.
- Does NOT replace contractual clauses; it operationalizes contract triggers into procurement and revenue processes.
- Owned by Finance (Revenue Operations) with procurement and legal co-ownership for vendor terms.

Definitions:
- Vendor Performance Incident (VPI): any event where vendor delivery or invoicing deviates from contract terms by an amount causing potential revenue impact > $10k or delay > 7 days.
- Billing Exception: invoice mismatch > 2% of expected amount or with unsupported line items.
- Service Delivery SLA: contractually defined metric (e.g., 99.5% availability for Dedicated capacity over a 30-day window).

Governance model and responsibilities:
1) Procurement team:
   - Primary owner for vendor selection, SOW acceptance, and PO issuance.
   - Maintain vendor profiles in VendorCentral (internal registry), including primary contact, backup contact, contract ID, and escalation matrix.
   - Tag every contract with RevRec-impact: none / low / medium / high.
2) Legal team:
   - Validate contract clauses for acceptance criteria, change-order flow, and termination rights that affect revenue timing.
3) Finance (RevOps):
   - Maintain revenue recognition mapping and enforce billing acceptance criteria prior to invoice posting.
   - Maintain the Vendor Performance Ledger (VPL) and calculate monthly adjustments.
4) Product/Engineering (for technical delivery):
   - Provide delivery evidence (deployment manifests, capacity proofs, release notes) required for milestone-based recognition.

KPI table (monthly cadence) — how we score vendors and the resulting action:
| KPI | Metric | Threshold (green) | Warning (amber) | Fail (red) | Action when amber | Action when red |
|-----|--------|------------------:|------------------:|-----------:|-------------------|------------------|
| SLA Compliance | % of required uptime/throughput | >= 99.5% | 98.0% — 99.49% | < 98.0% | Procurement notice + 1 remediation cycle | Trigger VPI, notify Finance, pause milestone recognition |
| Delivery Timeliness | % of milestones delivered on time | >= 95% | 80% — 94% | < 80% | Request recovery plan and ETA | Escalate to Legal / Contract remedy evaluation |
| Invoice Accuracy | Error rate vs PO | <= 2% | 2.1% — 5% | > 5% | Request corrected invoice; hold non-disputed lines | Withhold invoice payment; finance adjustment and possible credit notes |
| Support Responsiveness | MTTR for Sev2/Sev3 | <= 8 hours | 8 — 24 hours | > 24 hours | Escalation to vendor AM | Contractual SLA credit request + evaluate substitution |

Mapping vendor KPIs to revenue recognition and billing controls:
- Contracts with milestone-based revenue: Revenue is recognized only after product/engineering provides evidence artifacts (deployment manifests, signed acceptance, smoke test results). If vendor KPI is red for Delivery Timeliness or SLA Compliance that affects the milestone, Finance will delay recognition and record a potential deferral.
- Subscription / capacity reservations (Dedicated): If a vendor outage causes customer-facing capacity degradation for > 14 aggregated customer-days in a month, Finance will calculate billable credits per contract and adjust revenue in the month of impact.
- Invoicing exceptions: Any Billing Exception in excess of $5k triggers a temporary payment hold for the disputed amount and initiates a joint procurement/finance investigation.

Procedures (procurement -> finance handoff):
1) Prior to PO: Procurement tags the contract with RevRec-impact and uploads the contract to ContractVault with required milestone artifacts defined.
2) At delivery/milestone completion: Engineering uploads evidence to EvidenceStore and notifies Procurement + Finance via the VPL workflow.
3) Finance validates evidence and checks vendor KPIs for the trailing 30 days. If any relevant KPI is red, Finance issues a Revenue Delay Notice (RDN) and logs an adjustment.
4) Invoice processing: Finance compares invoice to PO and EvidenceStore. Discrepancies > 2% create a Billing Exception ticket in FinanceOps.
5) Month-end: Vendor Performance Ledger is reconciled; deferred revenue and credits are posted against GL accounts: 2200 (Deferred Vendor Services) and 5300 (Vendor Credits).

Escalation matrix and timelines:
- Day 0: Procurement files VPI and notifies Vendor AM and Finance.
- Day 3: Vendor must submit remediation plan and ETA.
- Day 7: If plan is insufficient or no progress, Legal and Revenue Operations hold a joint review and determine contract remedies (credits, penalties, or substitution).
- Day 14+: If unresolved and revenue impact threshold breached, Finance files a RevRec Impact Notification to the CFO and pauses affected revenue until remedied.

Example scenarios (operationalized):
- Scenario A: A Dedicated GPU vendor misses 10% of committed hours in a month (SLA Compliance = 89%). Action: VPI -> calculate per-customer credits; defer 100% of impacted month revenue for affected customers until crediting evidence posted; escalate to Legal for contract remedy assessment.
- Scenario B: A software vendor issues an invoice with unsupported license lines ($12k). Action: Payment hold on $12k, open Billing Exception, require vendor-corrected invoice and evidence of license entitlement.

Templates and checklist (appendix):
- Procurement pre-PO checklist: RevRec-impact tag, required evidence artifacts, acceptance tests, SLA clauses, primary contact, backup contact, billing cadence.
- Evidence artifact list (for milestone recognition): deployment manifest, test run IDs, signed acceptance email (product manager), smoke-test logs, capacity allocation receipts.
- Finance validation checklist: PO match, EvidenceStore confirmation, KPI check (VPL snapshot), invoice metadata verification, GL mapping, tax treatment confirmation.

Reporting and auditability:
- VPL is reconciled weekly and a monthly Vendor Performance Report is published to the Finance-Procurement dashboard.
- All evidence artifacts are retained for 7 years in ContractVault (as required for audits).
- Changes to thresholds or RevRec-impact categorizations must be approved by Head of RevOps and Procurement Director.

Change control and review cadence:
- This guideline is reviewed quarterly by the cross-functional Vendor Governance Committee.
- Emergency changes (for regulatory or major customer contract impacts) can be fast-tracked with CFO approval.

Contacts and ownership:

- Procurement lead: Carlos Mendez (carlos.m@redwood.com)
- Legal contact: Sana Iqbal (sana.iqbal@redwood.com)

Appendix A — Sample GL posting entries (narrative):
- On deferral: DR 4000 Contract Revenue (reversal) / CR 2200 Deferred Vendor Services (deferred obligation)
- For vendor credit: DR 5300 Vendor Credits / CR 2100 Accounts Payable

Revision history:
- 2025-04-11: Initial draft and committee review.
- 2025-08-02: Added Billing Exception thresholds and EvidenceStore integration notes.
- 2026-02-14: Updated SLA thresholds and introduced VPI definition (this published revision).

Disclaimer: This document operationalizes how procurement and finance treat vendor delivery when there is a material revenue or billing impact. It does not override signed contract terms; in the event of contradiction, Legal-approved contract language governs.
